decision_record.description: Retention-preservation declaration (owner-approved 2026-10-25; v3 item-enumerated contract owner-approved 2026-10-27). Set by the closeout gate; at retirement every declared slot's carrier is verified — card-id anchor + per-item handle together in the SAME committed, branch-reachable carrier — before a completed card is deleted. null on legacy cards that predate the gate. The version-1 (v1/v2 entries) shape is LEGACY: still storable/readable for in-flight cards and honored at retirement only in the routine case (no decision items); NEW closeouts declare version 3 only (one slot per decision item; empty items = the routine attestation).

anyOf.description: No decision_record: cards that have not closed out under the retention gate carry decision_record: null (the payload default), and legacy cards that predate the gate keep null — the retirement gate treats null as the legacy compatibility case (refused iff decision items are present). Validated explicitly here because anyOf is ANDed with the property's type union: without a null branch, both object alternatives would reject the default value.

Legacy v1/v2 shape (entries of kind commit | artifact | routine, optional carries excerpts). Retired: the excerpt-coverage machinery no longer runs; a decision-bearing legacy record must re-closeout under version 3.

revision.description: Commit sha or resolvable revision carrying the decision content. Omitted = search reachable commit messages for the marker. Must not start with "-" (option-injection guard: the retirement verifier passes it to git as a positional).

marker.description: Content marker verified in the commit message or a blob at that committed revision. Defaults to the card id. Proves presence only — it covers NO decision-class field. Must not start with "-" (option-injection guard: the retirement verifier hands it to git as a search pattern).

carries.description: Legacy v2 coverage declaration: map of decision-class field name to a verbatim single-line excerpt from that field's content. Retired with the v2 gate; kept so stored v2 records remain schema-valid.

path.description: Repo-relative durable file (docs/checkpoints/, researches/decisions/, researches/sources/, docs/planning/) carrying the card-id back-reference.

revision.description: Commit sha or resolvable revision whose committed blob must contain the marker. Omitted = search reachable revisions of the path. Must not start with "-" (option-injection guard).

marker.description: Back-reference string verified in the committed blob. Defaults to the card id. Proves presence only — it covers NO decision-class field. Must not start with "-" (option-injection guard).

carries.description: Legacy v2 coverage declaration (retired; kept for stored-record schema validity).

note.description: Attestation that nothing decision-class needs preserving; must be the only entry and must not contradict explicit decision-class card fields.

anyOf.description: v3 item-enumerated contract: ONE SLOT PER DECISION ITEM. Items are enumerated mechanically from the card (every owner note, every non-empty open question, the measured outcome, and every NON-PROCESS review signal — a review that resolved the card to completed is a process record). Empty items is the routine attestation, valid exactly when the card carries no decision items. The closeout gate additionally enforces what draft-07 cannot express: per-item handle binding (verbatim handles drawn from that item's own content), the canonical curated/sanitized label (decision-item: <task-id>#<item-id> (<disposition>)), required provenance on owner-decision and sanitized slots, duplicate-id refusal, and the add-only amendment rule for re-closeouts.

id.description: Stable CONTENT-BOUND item identity within the task: owner_notes[fnv1a:<hash>] | open_questions[fnv1a:<hash>] | measured_outcome[fnv1a:<hash>] | last_review[fnv1a:<hash>] | task_reviewed[fnv1a:<hash>] — <hash> is an FNV-1a digest of the item's own text; duplicate identical items carry a per-content occurrence suffix (.2, .3, ...; the first copy has none — never array position; reordering items changes no id, while an in-place content replacement mints a new id and refuses at retirement until declared). Must not start with "-", contain "#", or span lines (gate-enforced — the id is embedded in the carrier label the verifier searches for).

disposition.description: verbatim = the carrier carries the item's own text (handle = a verbatim single line of it, mechanically containment-checked). curated = the carrier carries a labeled useful summary (handle = the canonical item label; semantic fidelity is author + reviewer). sanitized = like curated but with sensitive material deliberately withheld (provenance must name what was omitted and the authority for it).

revision.description: Commit sha or resolvable revision whose message or blob at that committed revision must carry the anchor + handle. Omitted = search reachable commit messages (the landing-commit body pattern). Must not start with "-" (option-injection guard).

path.description: Repo-relative durable file (docs/checkpoints/, researches/decisions/, researches/sources/, docs/planning/) whose committed blob must carry the card-id anchor + this item's handle.

revision.description: Commit sha or resolvable revision whose committed blob is checked. Omitted = search reachable revisions of the path. Must not start with "-" (option-injection guard).

handle.description: The per-item representation. verbatim: a verbatim single line drawn from that item's own content, >= 24 chars trimmed, not the card id, no leading dash (gate-enforced). curated/sanitized: EXACTLY the canonical label 'decision-item: <task-id>#<item-id> (<disposition>)' (gate-enforced) — its presence in an anchored committed carrier means labeled content sits there; whether that content is a USEFUL, faithful representation is author + reviewer judgment, never the gate.

provenance.description: Who, when, where recorded. REQUIRED (gate-enforced) for owner-decision items (owner_notes[…]) and for sanitized items. For curated/sanitized representations it must be a CITED reference, never an invented or AI-paraphrased owner statement.

note.description: Free-form record-level note (e.g. why an amendment was declared).

recurrence.description: Optional recurrence-signature block. OPTIONAL on every card: legacy cards carry no block (backward-compat). When present, REQUIRES the two-level identity (recurrence_id = exact-defect collapse key; symptom_class_id = immutable/versioned taxonomy id) AND the acknowledgement pair (recurrence_count / last_acknowledged_count), and carries non-identity evidence[] plus a bounded aliases[]/supersession list. The cross-field invariant recurrence_count >= last_acknowledged_count is enforced by the validator script (draft-07 cannot express it).

recurrence_id.description: Stable, explicit identity of ONE underlying defect. The actual collapse key. Authored when a defect is first recognized as recurring.

symptom_class_id.description: Immutable, versioned taxonomy identifier aggregating the CLASS of symptom (e.g. recurrence.v1/<class>).

recurrence_count.description: Total observations of this recurrence_id. The ack-pair invariant (recurrence_count >= last_acknowledged_count) is enforced by the validator script.

last_acknowledged_count.description: recurrence_count at last disposition adjudication. A recurrence_count above this marks the entry unadjudicated (release-enforcement semantics, a later slice).

evidence.description: Non-identity observations attached to the entry: paths, claim_ids, affected capabilities, outcomes, commit subjects/ranges, later root-cause findings.

kind.description: Discriminator for the evidence entry (e.g. path, claim_id, capability, outcome, commit_subject, commit_range).

ref.description: The evidence locator/value (a path, a claim id, a capability name, a commit subject/range, etc.).

aliases.description: Bounded alias/supersession reconciliation for an identity that must be re-pointed after later evidence.

recurrence_id.description: An alternate or superseded recurrence_id reconciled into this canonical entry.

superseded.description: True when this alias has been superseded by the canonical recurrence_id.
